Working principle · 3D interactive

How the S-1688 cleans your stencil

Drag the 3D view to rotate it. The stencil goes into the chamber, rotating spray rods wash both sides with solvent or water-based detergent, the liquid is filtered and recycled, then compressed air dries it.

01 · Load the stencil

Put the stencil into the cleaning room, set clean and dry time, close the front door.

02 · Rotating spray wash

Upper and lower spray rods rotate 360° and spray solvent or water-based detergent onto both sides.

03 · Filter & recycle

3-level filtration (100 µm / 50 µm / 1 µm) keeps the liquid clean and recycled each cycle.

04 · Air dry

Compressed air dries the stencil; open the door and the clean stencil is ready.

The hidden cost of manual stencil cleaning

Wasted liquid and damaged workers are taxing your line

Every drop of wasted cleaning liquid, every operator exposed to chemicals, and every blocked aperture costs money. A pneumatic stencil cleaner changes that math.

Wasting cleaning liquid

Manual cleaning and poor filtration waste solvent and water-based detergent.

Chemicals damage workers

Hand exposure to cleaning liquid puts operators at risk.

Sewage pollutes the earth

Uncontrolled discharge of contaminated cleaning liquid damages the environment.

Blocked apertures

Residue left in stencil apertures causes paste misprint and rework.

Manual results vary

Hand-cleaning quality depends on the operator, batch and shift.

Fire and detonation risk

Electric cleaning equipment with flammable solvents carries ignition risk.

Installation guide

Install and commission the S-1688

Reference procedure based on the S-1688 operation and maintenance manual. Full documentation ships with the machine.

01 · Site preparation

Place the machine on a solid, flat, clean floor with enough space for installation, spare parts and maintenance.

02 · Utilities

Connect the main air hose (0.5–0.7 MPa) and the exhaust vent to an outer hose; confirm the vent is sealed firmly.

03 · Liquid & filters

Fill the cleaning tank with solvent or water-based detergent (non-foam); check the 3-level filters.

04 · Pre-run check

Check valves, filters, doors and covers, and that no sundries are left in the machine.

05 · Clean test

Load a stencil, set clean and dry times, press Start and verify the result.

Technical evaluation FAQ

Questions buyers ask before ordering

What does the S-1688 clean?

It cleans solder paste stencils, red glue stencils, resin masks and copper masks, removing residue with solvent or water-based detergent.

Why full pneumatic?

The machine is driven entirely by compressed air — no electric power — so there is no ignition source near flammable cleaning liquids. That reduces fire and detonation risk.

How does the cleaning process work?

Load the stencil, set clean and dry time, close the front door and press Start. Rotating spray rods wash both sides, the liquid passes through 3-level filtration and is recycled, then air drying finishes the cycle.

What filtration does it use?

3-level filter: 100 µm for larger materials, 50 µm for labels and screws, and 1 µm for solder paste balls — keeping the liquid clean each cycle.

How long does a cycle take?

Recommended clean time is 3–10 minutes and dry time 3–8 minutes, controlled by mechanical timers.

How do I get a price and delivery time?

Email info@smthelp.com or WhatsApp +86 136 0256 2576 with your stencil types, cleaning liquid and volume. Quotation and delivery schedule are provided after technical confirmation — typically the same working day.
